back: The old order in France before 1789: absolute monarchy, three unequal estates and a system of privileges.

front: What were the cahiers de doléances?
back: Lists of grievances drawn up in the spring of 1789 and sent to Versailles with the deputies.

front: When did the Estates-General open, and when had it last met?
back: 5 May 1789 at Versailles; it had last met in 1614.

front: What happened on 17 June and 20 June 1789?
back: The Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly (17 June) and swore the Tennis Court Oath (20 June).

front: When was the Bastille stormed, and why did it matter?
back: 14 July 1789; the king lost control of Paris and the Assembly was saved.

front: What did the August Decrees (4-11 August 1789) do?
back: Abolished feudal dues, the tithe, privileges and the sale of offices in law.
Women of Paris marched to Versailles over bread, and the royal family was brought to Paris.

front: Why did Calonne's reform plan fail in 1787?
back: The Assembly of Notables, who would have paid the land tax, refused it and said only an Estates-General could agree.

front: Why did voting by order or by head matter in 1789?
back: By order the clergy and nobles could outvote the Third Estate; by head its larger number of deputies would count.
